title: Can, may, must: ability and obligation
objectives: Say what you know how to do with marunong and what you're able to do with kaya
Ask for and give permission with puwede; forbid with bawal and huwag
Express need and obligation with kailangan and dapat
Control which pronoun form (ako vs ko) each of these words takes

grammar.title: Marunong, kaya, alam: three kinds of 'can/know'
grammar.explanation:
English 'can' and 'know' split three ways in Tagalog.

Marunong = know how to, have the skill. It takes an ang-form actor plus the linker, then the basic verb form: 'Marunong akong lumangoy' — I know how to swim. 'Marunong ka bang magmaneho?' — Do you know how to drive? With a language or subject it takes ng: 'Marunong siya ng Ingles.'

Kaya = can manage it, be physically or practically able. It takes a NG-form actor: 'Kaya kong buhatin ito' — I can lift this. 'Hindi ko kaya' — I can't (manage it). Kaya is about capacity in the moment; marunong is about learned skill. You may be marunong lumangoy but, exhausted, hindi mo kayang lumangoy ngayon.

Alam = know a fact or piece of information, never a skill: 'Alam ko ang sagot' — I know the answer. 'Alam mo ba kung nasaan siya?' — Do you know where he is? Mixing these up is a classic learner error: for skills use marunong, for facts use alam.

examples.en: I know how to cook adobo.

examples.tl: Hindi ko kayang buhatin ang kahon. Ang bigat!
examples.en: I can't lift the box. It's so heavy!

examples.tl: Alam ko ang pangalan niya, pero hindi ko alam ang trabaho niya.
examples.en: I know his name, but I don't know his job.

examples.tl: Marunong ka ba ng Tagalog? — Konti lang po.
examples.en: Do you know Tagalog? — Just a little.

grammar.title: Puwede, bawal, huwag: permission and prohibition
grammar.explanation:
Puwede (often spelled pwede) covers 'may' and 'is it okay': 'Puwede ba akong umupo dito?' — May I sit here? 'Puwede mo bang buksan ang bintana?' — Could you open the window? Notice both patterns: with an actor-focus verb the actor is ang-form (puwede AKONG umupo); with an object-focus verb the actor is ng-form (puwede MO bang...). Answers: 'Puwede' / 'Oo, puwede naman' or 'Hindi puwede.'

Bawal means forbidden — you see it on signs all over Manila: 'Bawal tumawid' (no crossing), 'Bawal pumarada dito' (no parking here), 'Bawal ang pagkain sa loob' (no food inside). Structure: bawal + basic verb, or bawal ang + noun.

Huwag is the word for negative commands — 'don't'. It replaces hindi in commands and takes the linker on the pronoun: 'Huwag kang tumakbo!' — Don't run! 'Huwag mong kainin iyan!' — Don't eat that! Using hindi for a command ('Hindi ka tumakbo') is a common mistake; commands need huwag.

examples.tl: Huwag kang mag-ingay, natutulog ang baby.
examples.en: Don't be noisy, the baby is sleeping.

examples.tl: Puwede mo bang hintayin ako? — Sige, puwede.
examples.en: Can you wait for me? — Sure, no problem.

grammar.title: Kailangan and dapat: need and should
grammar.explanation:
Kailangan = need/must. With a verb, the actor takes the NG-form plus linker: 'Kailangan kong mag-aral' — I need to study. 'Kailangan mong umuwi na' — you need to go home now. With a noun, kailangan takes ng like gusto did in A1: 'Kailangan ko ng tulong' — I need help. 'Kailangan namin ng tatlong upuan.'

Dapat = should/ought to, a matter of what is right or advisable rather than hard necessity. It takes an ANG-form actor with the linker: 'Dapat kang magpahinga' — you should rest. 'Dapat akong matulog nang maaga.' In practice you will also hear 'dapat ay' and bare 'dapat + verb' ('Dapat mag-aral ka'); all are fine.

A quick map of which pronoun form these little words take with verbs: ng-form (ko/mo/niya): gusto, ayaw, kaya, kailangan. Ang-form (ako/ka/siya): puwede, marunong, dapat. When in doubt, notice the pattern in examples rather than translating from English.

examples.tl: Kailangan kong tapusin ito bago mag-alas-singko.
examples.en: I need to finish this before five o'clock.

examples.tl: Kailangan namin ng mas malaking mesa.
Dapat kang uminom ng maraming tubig araw-araw.
examples.en: You should drink lots of water every day.

examples.tl: Hindi mo dapat kainin iyan. Sira na yata.
examples.en: You shouldn't eat that. It seems spoiled.

example.en: I know how to ride a bike.

vocab.note: kaya + ng-actor: kaya ko, kaya mo

example.en: You can do it!
May I sit here?

vocab.note: kailangan ko ng + noun; kailangan kong + verb

example.en: I need new shoes.
You should sleep early.

example.tl: Bawal kumain sa loob ng jeep.
example.en: Eating inside the jeep is not allowed.
Don't be sad.

vocab.note: alam ko, alam mo — never for skills

example.en: I don't know the answer.
Do you know how to swim?
He drives to work.
We ride bikes every Sunday.

example.tl: Binuhat niya ang mabigat na kahon.
example.en: He lifted the heavy box.

example.tl: Marunong siyang magsalita ng tatlong wika.
example.en: She knows how to speak three languages.
I don't know how to dance.
He knows how to play the guitar.

example.tl: Bawal tumawid dito. Doon sa tulay.
example.en: You can't cross here. Over there at the footbridge.

example.tl: Puwede ka bang tumulong sa akin?
example.en: Can you help me?
Try our sinigang!
Thanks for your help.

example.tl: Wala pa akong lisensya sa pagmamaneho.
example.en: I don't have a driver's license yet.
How many languages do you know?

example.tl: May gitara ba kayo sa bahay?
example.en: Do you have a guitar at home?
This box is so heavy!
My bag is heavy today.
This is light. I can manage it.
Be careful on the road, okay?
Don't make noise in the library.

vocab.note: Sandali lang po = just a moment

example.tl: Sandali lang, tatapusin ko lang ito.
example.en: Just a moment, I'll just finish this.

dialogue.title: At the community pool
dialogue.context: Ramon brings his officemate Grace to the neighborhood pool for the first time.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.tl: Wow, ang ganda ng pool! Puwede ba tayong lumangoy agad?
lines.en: Wow, the pool is beautiful! Can we swim right away?

lines.speaker: Ramon
lines.tl: Sandali lang. Kailangan muna nating magbayad sa counter.
lines.en: Just a moment. We need to pay at the counter first.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.en: Ah, okay. How much is it?

lines.speaker: Ramon
lines.tl: Singkwenta pesos lang. O, marunong ka bang lumangoy?
lines.en: Just fifty pesos. So, do you know how to swim?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.tl: Konti lang. Hindi ko kayang lumangoy sa malalim.
lines.en: Just a little. I can't swim in the deep part.

lines.speaker: Ramon
lines.tl: Okay lang. Dapat kang manatili sa mababaw na parte.
lines.en: That's fine. You should stay in the shallow part.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.en: Are there rules here — things not allowed?

lines.speaker: Ramon
lines.tl: Oo. Bawal tumakbo sa gilid ng pool, at bawal kumain sa tubig.
lines.en: Yes. No running at the poolside, and no eating in the water.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.tl: Puwede bang magdala ng pagkain sa mga mesa doon?
lines.en: Can we bring food to the tables over there?

lines.speaker: Ramon
lines.tl: Puwede naman. Pero huwag mong iwanan ang gamit mo. Walang bantay.
lines.en: That's allowed. But don't leave your things. There's no attendant.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.tl: Sige. Ay, kailangan ko pala ng swimming cap!
lines.en: Okay. Oh, it turns out I need a swimming cap!

lines.speaker: Ramon
lines.tl: May tindahan sa tabi ng counter. Bumili ka muna doon.
lines.en: There's a shop next to the counter. Go buy one there first.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.tl: Salamat! Tapos, tuturuan mo ako, ha? Gusto kong matutong lumangoy.
lines.en: Thanks! Then you'll teach me, okay? I want to learn to swim.

lines.speaker: Ramon
lines.en: Of course. You can do it!

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'know how to (a skill)'?
exercises.explain: Marunong is for learned skills; alam is for facts; kaya is about capacity to manage something.

exercises.prompt: Marunong ___ lumangoy. (I know how to swim.)
exercises.explain: Marunong takes an ang-form actor with the linker -ng: marunong akong lumangoy.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'I can't lift this' (it's too heavy)?
exercises.explain: Physical capacity is kaya with a ng-form actor: hindi ko kayang buhatin ito.

exercises.prompt: ___ ko ang sagot, pero hindi ako marunong magpaliwanag. (I KNOW the answer...)
exercises.explain: Knowing a fact is alam; marunong is reserved for skills.

exercises.prompt: You want to ask permission to sit down. Which is correct?
exercises.explain: Puwede takes an ang-form actor: puwede ba akong umupo. Kaya would question your physical ability, dapat your obligation.

exercises.tl: Bawal pumarada dito. May towing po.
choices: No parking here — cars get towed.
exercises.explain: Bawal pumarada = parking is forbidden; may towing warns that vehicles are towed.

exercises.prompt: ___ kang tumakbo sa gilid ng pool! (Don't run at the poolside!)
exercises.explain: Commands are negated with huwag, and the pronoun takes the linker: huwag kang tumakbo.

exercises.prompt: 'Kailangan ko ___ tulong' vs 'Kailangan ko ___ umalis'. Choose the pair of missing words.
exercises.explain: With a noun, kailangan takes ng (kailangan ko ng tulong); with a verb, the actor gets the linker: kailangan kong umalis.

exercises.prompt: You should drink lots of water every day.
exercises.answer: Dapat kang uminom ng maraming tubig araw-araw.
accept: Dapat kang uminom ng maraming tubig araw-araw
Dapat kang uminom ng maraming tubig
Dapat uminom ka ng maraming tubig araw-araw
Araw-araw dapat kang uminom ng maraming tubig
exercises.explain: Dapat takes an ang-form actor with the linker: dapat kang uminom; maraming tubig = lots of water.

exercises.prompt: Hindi ako marunong sumayaw, pero marunong akong kumanta.
exercises.answer: I don't know how to dance, but I know how to sing.
accept: I don't know how to dance, but I know how to sing
I can't dance but I can sing
I don't know how to dance but I can sing
exercises.explain: Marunong + verb = know how to; pero contrasts the two skills.

exercises.prompt: Your friend looks exhausted. The most natural advice is:
exercises.explain: Dapat gives advice: you should rest. Bawal would forbid it; marunong/kaya talk about skill and capacity.

exercises.prompt: Can you help me? I need to finish this before five.
exercises.answer: Puwede ka bang tumulong sa akin? Kailangan kong tapusin ito bago mag-alas-singko.
accept: Puwede ka bang tumulong sa akin? Kailangan kong tapusin ito bago mag-alas-singko
Puwede mo ba akong tulungan? Kailangan kong tapusin ito bago mag-alas-singko
Pwede ka bang tumulong sa akin? Kailangan kong tapusin ito bago mag-alas-singko
exercises.explain: Puwede + ang-actor (ka) + ba + linker for the request; kailangan + ng-actor with linker (kong) + object-focus tapusin for the deadline.

exercises.prompt: Marunong siyang ___ ng gitara. (She knows how to play the guitar.)
exercises.explain: After marunong + linker the verb appears in its basic -um- form: tumugtog ng gitara.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is wrong, and would make a Tagalog speaker do a double take?
exercises.explain: Kaya takes a ng-form actor: kaya KONG magmaneho. The other three correctly pair puwede/dapat with ang-forms and kailangan with the ng-form.
